newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Chubais says pension arrears fully repaid.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chubais says pension arrears fully repaid.

text.p: First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Thursday the government had repaid all its debts to Russian pensioners as part of its drive to resolve the country's deep-seated social problems.
"Budget obligations (to pensioners) have been met 100 percent," Chubais told a cabinet meeting in remarks broadcast on Russian television.
"We have every reason to say that the task set by President Boris Yeltsin has been implemented fully and on time," he added.
Earlier this year Yeltsin ordered the government to pay off arrears on old age pensions by July 1 and to take steps to ensure that delays do not recur in future.
Ministers have blamed poor tax collection for the pension and wage arrears that have helped fuel social discontent across the vast Russian Federation.

Chubais, who is also finance minister, said the last money transfer of 2.75 trillion roubles ($477.3 million) in pension arrears was made on Wednesday. He did not say how much money the pensioners had been owed.
He added that Russia's Savings Bank and commercial banks would be working all weekend to deliver the money to pensioners.
"By July 1 not a single rouble will be owed to a single pensioner," said Chubais, a pro-market reformer.
The ministers have said that in future timely pension payments will hinge partly on success in cutting other spending, including a wide array of Soviet-era welfare benefits.

Earlier this week the State Duma lower house of parliament rejected the cabinet's planned budget squeeze, saying cuts would hurt poorer Russians struggling to make ends, but ministers have said they will press on anyway.
